```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "png", dpi = 300)

run_hash <- "60bac5f5db60632f"
res_all <- readRDS(here::here(
  "results", "data", run_hash, "aggregation_summary_default.rds"
))$aggregation$summary

# Method x scenario rows where every replicate errored carry no information; they are dropped and named below.
failed <- res_all |> filter(prop_error == 1)
res <- res_all |> filter(prop_error < 1)

method_labels <- c(
  classical_ml = "Classical ML",
  multiple_imputation = "MI + closed form",
  reweighting = "Reweighting",
  LSPIM = "LSPIM"
)
method_colours <- c(
  "Classical ML" = "#0072B2",
  "MI + closed form" = "#E69F00",
  "Reweighting" = "#009E73",
  "LSPIM" = "#CC79A7"
)
dropout_labels <- c(half_missing = "Half-missing", three_obs_minimum = "Three observations minimum")

# Log scenarios: only the large (-2.42, 1.95) and small (-0.385, 0.31) crossing pairs and the null are reported.
is_pair <- function(b1, b3, p1, p3) abs(b1 - p1) < 1e-6 & abs(b3 - p3) < 0.005
res <- res |>
  mutate(
    log_effect = case_when(
      time_trend != "log" ~ NA_character_,
      beta1 == 0 & beta3 == 0 ~ "null",
      is_pair(beta1, beta3, -2.42, 1.948) ~ "large",
      is_pair(beta1, beta3, -0.385, 0.310) ~ "small",
      TRUE ~ "excluded"
    )
  ) |>
  filter(is.na(log_effect) | log_effect != "excluded") |>
  mutate(
    method = factor(method_labels[method], levels = method_labels),
    dropout = factor(dropout_labels[dropout_mechanism], levels = dropout_labels),
    n = factor(n),
    effect = case_when(
      time_trend == "linear" & beta3 == 0 ~ "null (beta3 = 0)",
      time_trend == "linear" ~ paste0("beta3 = ", signif(beta3, 3)),
      log_effect == "null" ~ "null (identical arms)",
      log_effect == "large" ~ "large (beta1 = -2.42, beta3 = 1.95)",
      log_effect == "small" ~ "small (beta1 = -0.385, beta3 = 0.31)"
    ),
    effect = factor(effect, levels = c(
      "beta3 = 0.22", "beta3 = 0.035", "null (beta3 = 0)",
      "large (beta1 = -2.42, beta3 = 1.95)", "small (beta1 = -0.385, beta3 = 0.31)", "null (identical arms)"
    )),
    # Short column labels for the tables
    eff_short = case_when(
      beta3 == 0 ~ "0",
      log_effect == "large" ~ "large",
      log_effect == "small" ~ "small",
      TRUE ~ as.character(signif(beta3, 3))
    ),
    eff_short = factor(eff_short, levels = c("0.22", "0.035", "large", "small", "0")),
    drop_short = ifelse(dropout_mechanism == "half_missing", "HM", "3O")
  )

lin <- res |> filter(time_trend == "linear")
logt <- res |> filter(time_trend == "log")
# LSPIM gives only a test decision, so it has no MSE or coverage.
lin_est <- lin |> filter(method != "LSPIM")

# Three significant digits, keeping trailing zeros; NA as a dash.
fmt3 <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "-", formatC(signif(x, 3), format = "fg", digits = 3, flag = "#"))
fmt3 <- Vectorize(fmt3)
fmt3_trim <- function(x) sub("\\.$", "", fmt3(x))

# Wide table: rows n x method, columns dropout x effect.
metric_table <- function(df, metric, caption) {
  df |>
    mutate(value = fmt3_trim(.data[[metric]]), col = paste(drop_short, eff_short, sep = ": ")) |>
    arrange(drop_short != "HM", eff_short) |>
    select(n, method, col, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) |>
    arrange(n, method) |>
    rename(Method = method) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = caption, align = "l")
}

metric_plot <- function(df, metric, ylab, hline = NULL, log_y = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(
    x = n, y = .data[[metric]], colour = method, shape = effect, linetype = effect,
    group = interaction(method, effect)
  )) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~dropout) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = method_colours, drop = TRUE) +
    labs(x = "Number of clusters", y = ylab, colour = "Method", shape = "Effect", linetype = "Effect") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
  if (n_distinct(df$effect) == 1) p <- p + guides(shape = "none", linetype = "none")
  if (!is.null(hline)) p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = hline, linetype = "dotted")
  if (log_y) p <- p + scale_y_log10()
  p
}

status_levels <- c(
  prop_converged_ok = "Converged",
  prop_converged_warning = "Converged (warning)",
  prop_converged_singular = "Converged (singular)",
  prop_not_converged = "Not converged",
  prop_error = "Error"
)

# Convergence pooled over effect sizes: convergence barely depends on beta3.
convergence_long <- function(df) {
  df |>
    group_by(method, dropout, n) |>
    summarise(across(all_of(names(status_levels)), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(names(status_levels)), names_to = "status", values_to = "prop") |>
    mutate(status = factor(status_levels[status], levels = status_levels))
}

convergence_plot <- function(df) {
  ggplot(convergence_long(df), aes(x = n, y = prop, fill = status)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    facet_grid(dropout ~ method, labeller = label_wrap_gen(18)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#009E73", "#56B4E9", "#F0E442", "#D55E00", "#999999"), drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Number of clusters", y = "Proportion of replicates", fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
}

lambda_table <- function(df, caption) {
  df |>
    filter(method == "MI + closed form") |>
    mutate(value = fmt3_trim(mean_mi_lambda_beta3), col = paste(drop_short, eff_short, sep = ": ")) |>
    arrange(drop_short != "HM", eff_short) |>
    select(n, col, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = value) |>
    arrange(n) |>
    knitr::kable(caption = caption, align = "l")
}
```

# Overview methods

| Method | Configuration |
|-------|-----------------------------------------|
| Classical ML | `lme4::lmer`, ML (REML = FALSE); Wald $t$ test on $\beta_3$ with $N - 2$ df |
| MI + closed form | `mice` `2l.pmm`, 3 imputations, `maxit` = 10; closed form (CbC) per imputation, pooled with Rubin's rules; Wald $t$ test on $\beta_3$ with Barnard-Rubin df (complete-data df $N - 2$) |
| Reweighting | Closed form, reweighted until max $\Delta\beta < 10^{-6}$, at most 30 iterations; Wald $t$ test on $\beta_3$ with $N - 2$ df |
| LSPIM | Pseudo-score GEE model (Firth-penalised, Ford-Westgate small-sample sandwich), fitted with an improved algorithm; Holm-adjusted test that the per-visit treatment effects differ; run at every $n$ |

: Configuration of the methods; $N$ is the number of clusters in the fit. {tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

| Method | "Not converged" when |
|-------|-----------------------------------------|
| Classical ML | optimizer code $\neq 0$ or an lme4 convergence message (e.g. max\|grad\| $> 0.002$) |
| MI + closed form | never; a failed fit in any imputation counts as an error |
| Reweighting | the loop reaches 30 iterations without meeting the $\Delta\beta$ criterion |
| LSPIM | the penalised GEE does not converge (fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1) |

: Definition of "not converged" per method. {tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

Each replicate gets exactly one of five convergence statuses, checked in this order:

| Status | Meaning |
|-------|-----------------------------------------|
| Error | The fit failed (no estimates); excluded from all metrics. |
| Not converged | Fit returned estimates, but the method's convergence criterion (table above) was not met. |
| Converged (singular) | Converged, but the random-effects covariance is at the boundary (smallest eigenvalue $\leq 10^{-6}$, or the final $D$ repaired to positive definite). |
| Converged (warning) | Converged and not singular, but a warning was raised (e.g. lme4's boundary message at its looser tolerance; for reweighting NaNs in an intermediate iteration; for LSPIM the combined covariance $V$ repaired to the nearest positive semi-definite matrix). |
| Converged | Converged, not singular, no warning. |

: Convergence statuses. {tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

-   All tests at $\alpha = 0.05$; coverage of the 95% $t$ interval for $\beta_3$.
-   All statuses except "error" are kept in all metrics.
-   LSPIM gives only a test decision, no estimate of $\beta_3$: it appears in the type I error, power, convergence and computation time results, not in MSE, coverage or fraction of missing information. Its errors and warnings are described in the appendix.

```{r}
if (nrow(failed) > 0) {
  cat(
    "::: callout-warning\n## Missing results\n\n",
    "All replicates errored for: ",
    paste(unique(method_labels[failed$method]), collapse = ", "),

  )
```

# Simulation setup

Linear model, $t_j = j = 0, \dots, 11$: $$ y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 Treatment_i + \beta_2 t_j + \beta_3 Treatment_i \times t_j + b_{0i} + b_{1i} t_j + \varepsilon_{ij} $$

Log model, $t_j = j = 0, \dots, 11$: $$ y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 Treatment_i + \beta_2 \log(1 + t_j) + \beta_3 Treatment_i \times \log(1 + t_j) + b_{0i} + b_{1i} \log(1 + t_j) + \varepsilon_{ij} $$

In both models $(b_{0i}, b_{1i})^\top \sim N(0, D)$ with $D = \begin{pmatrix} d_{11} & d_{12} \\ d_{12} & d_{22} \end{pmatrix}$ and $\varepsilon_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$.

| Effect | Symbol | Linear | Log |
|---------------|------|-------------|--------------------------|
| Intercept | $\beta_0$ | 2.4562 | 2.4562 |
| Treatment effect | $\beta_1$ | 0 | $-2.42$ / $-0.385$ / 0 |
| Time effect | $\beta_2$ | 0.2792 | 1.2359 |
| Treatment $\times$ time | $\beta_3$ | 0.22 / 0.035 / 0 | 1.948 / 0.310 / 0 |
| Random intercept variance | $d_{11}$ | 7.3174 | 7.3174 |
| Random slope variance | $d_{22}$ | 0.2239 | 4.3875 |
| Random effects covariance | $d_{12}$ | $-0.4985$ | $-2.2067$ |
| Residual variance | $\sigma^2$ | 3.1508 | 3.1508 |

: Data-generating parameters; a / b / c gives the values of the large, small and null effect. {tbl-colwidths="[36,10,24,30]"}

-   Linear parameters taken from the toenail data ($\beta_3 = 0.035$); $\beta_3 = 0.22$ added as a larger effect.
-   Log parameters: $\beta_2$, $d_{22}$ and $d_{12}$ rescaled by $11 / \log 12$, so the rise and the slope variance at $t = 11$ match the linear scenario.
-   Log crossing: arms cross at $t \approx 2.5$; the treatment difference at $t = 11$ equals that of the linear scenario with $\beta_3 = 0.22$ (large) or $0.035$ (small).
-   Log null: identical arms ($\beta_1 = \beta_3 = 0$).

| Variable | Value |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Number of clusters | 10, 20, 50, 100, 1000 |
| Number of repeated measures | 12 |
| Missingness pattern | "Half-missing" (HM): half of the clusters have no missingness, the other half have a uniform probability to keep 1--11 observations; dropout is monotone. |
| | "Three observations minimum" (3O): as half-missing, but with at least three observations per cluster. |
| Simulations per scenario | 5000 |

: Simulation design. {tbl-colwidths="[31,69]"}

```{r}
#| label: fig-log-profiles
#| fig-cap: "Mean profiles per arm for the log time trend, from the simulation parameters."
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-pos: "H"
log_par <- data.frame(
  effect = factor(
    c("large (beta1 = -2.42, beta3 = 1.95)", "small (beta1 = -0.385, beta3 = 0.31)", "null (identical arms)"),
    levels = c("large (beta1 = -2.42, beta3 = 1.95)", "small (beta1 = -0.385, beta3 = 0.31)", "null (identical arms)")
  ),
  beta1 = c(-2.42, -0.385, 0),
  beta3 = c(2 * 0.22 * 11 / log(12), 2 * 0.035 * 11 / log(12), 0)
)
beta0 <- 2.4562
beta2 <- 0.2792 * 11 / log(12)
profiles <- merge(log_par, expand.grid(t = 0:11, arm = c("Control", "Treatment"))) |>
  mutate(mean_y = beta0 + beta2 * log1p(t) + (arm == "Treatment") * (beta1 + beta3 * log1p(t)))

ggplot(profiles, aes(x = t, y = mean_y, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~effect, labeller = label_wrap_gen(40)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 11, by = 2)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Control = "#555555", Treatment = "#D55E00")) +
  labs(x = "Time (t)", y = "Mean outcome", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Results - linear time trend

## Mean squared error of $\beta_3$

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lin-mse
metric_table(lin_est, "mse_beta3", "MSE of beta3 (HM = half-missing, 3O = three observations minimum; columns = true beta3).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lin-mse
#| fig-cap: "MSE of beta3 for the linear time trend (log scale)."
metric_plot(lin_est, "mse_beta3", "MSE (beta3)", log_y = TRUE)
```

-   MSE falls with the number of clusters at the same rate for all methods; the effect size hardly matters, and MSE is slightly lower under three observations minimum.
-   MI has the lowest MSE at $n = 10$ and $20$; from $n = 50$ onwards classical ML and reweighting are slightly better and nearly identical.

\newpage

## Type I error

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lin-t1e
metric_table(filter(lin, beta3 == 0), "type1_error", "Type I error rate of the interaction test (beta3 = 0).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lin-t1e
#| fig-cap: "Type I error rate for the linear time trend (dotted line: nominal 0.05)."
metric_plot(filter(lin, beta3 == 0), "type1_error", "Type I error rate", hline = 0.05)
```

-   Classical ML is still anti-conservative at small $n$ (about 0.10 at $n = 10$, 0.07--0.08 at $n = 20$) and close to nominal from $n = 50$.
-   Reweighting is slightly inflated at $n = 10$ and $20$ (about 0.06) and nominal from $n = 50$.
-   MI is at or slightly below nominal at every $n$ (about 0.04--0.05).
-   LSPIM is the most inflated at $n = 10$ (0.11--0.12) and still at $n = 20$ (about 0.08); from $n = 50$ onwards it is conservative (0.035--0.045).

\newpage

## Power

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lin-power
metric_table(filter(lin, beta3 != 0), "power", "Power of the interaction test.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lin-power
#| fig-cap: "Power for the linear time trend."
metric_plot(filter(lin, beta3 != 0), "power", "Power")
```

-   Classical ML has the highest power, then reweighting, then MI; at small $n$ the lead of classical ML partly reflects its type I error inflation.
-   For $\beta_3 = 0.22$ classical ML, reweighting and MI reach full power at $n = 1000$; for $\beta_3 = 0.035$ power stays low even at $n = 1000$ (0.13--0.17), lowest for MI.
-   LSPIM has much lower power than the other methods for a linear effect: for $\beta_3 = 0.22$ about 0.18--0.20 at $n = 100$ (others 0.40--0.53), 0.99 at $n = 1000$; for $\beta_3 = 0.035$ it stays near its type I error level. At $n = 10$ and $20$ its power mostly reflects its type I error inflation.

\newpage

## Coverage of $\beta_3$

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lin-cov
metric_table(lin_est, "coverage_beta3", "Coverage of the 95% t interval for beta3.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lin-cov
#| fig-cap: "Coverage of the 95% interval for beta3 for the linear time trend (dotted line: 0.95)."
metric_plot(lin_est, "coverage_beta3", "Coverage (beta3)", hline = 0.95)
```

-   Classical ML undercovers at small $n$ (about 0.90 at $n = 10$, 0.92--0.93 at $n = 20$) and is close to nominal from $n = 50$.
-   Reweighting is slightly below nominal at $n = 10$ and $20$ (0.94) and nominal from $n = 50$.
-   MI is at or slightly above nominal at every $n$ (0.95--0.96).

\newpage

## Convergence

```{r}
#| label: fig-lin-conv
#| fig-cap: "Convergence status for the linear time trend, pooled over effect sizes."
#| fig-height: 5
convergence_plot(lin)
```

-   Singular fits occur at $n = 10$ for classical ML, MI and reweighting at a similar rate (5--9%) and almost vanish from $n = 20$.
-   Reweighting and MI essentially always converge; reweighting has a small warning share at $n = 10$ and $20$.
-   Classical ML has a small "not converged" share at every $n$, which grows to about 26% at $n = 1000$. This is a false positive of lme4's absolute gradient check, which scales with the sample size: the flagged fits are kept in all metrics.
-   LSPIM: about 20% errors at $n = 10$, and almost all fits at $n = 10$ and $20$ carry a warning; see the appendix.

\newpage

## Computation time

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lin-time
metric_table(lin, "time_median_seconds", "Median computation time per replicate (seconds).")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lin-time
#| fig-cap: "Median computation time per replicate for the linear time trend (log scale)."
metric_plot(lin, "time_median_seconds", "Median time (seconds)", log_y = TRUE)
```

-   Classical ML is fastest from $n = 50$ onwards; at $n = 10$ and $20$ LSPIM is slightly faster.
-   MI is slowest up to $n = 100$ (1--2 seconds per replicate).
-   LSPIM is fast up to $n = 100$ (at most about 1 second) but grows roughly quadratically with $n$: at $n = 1000$ it is the slowest method (about 45--58 seconds), against about 14--17 seconds for MI and reweighting.

# Results - log time trend

-   MSE and coverage are not reported: the linear methods estimate a linear slope, which has no true value under the log trend.
-   Effect sizes: large ($\beta_1 = -2.42$, $\beta_3 = 1.95$), small ($\beta_1 = -0.385$, $\beta_3 = 0.31$).


# Suggested improvements

1.  Classical ML convergence: replace lme4's absolute gradient flag with a relative gradient check, to remove the false "not converged" at large $n$.

\newpage

# Appendix: LSPIM errors and warnings

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lspim-status
lspim_scenarios <- res_all |>
  filter(method == "LSPIM") |>
  distinct(scenario_id, n, dropout_mechanism)
lspim_files <- list.files(
  here::here("results", "data", run_hash),
  pattern = "_LSPIM_.*[.]rds$", full.names = TRUE
)
lspim_reps <- bind_rows(lapply(lspim_files, function(path) {
  readRDS(path)$results[, c("scenario_id", "convergence_status", "error_message")]
}))

lspim_outcomes <- c(
  ok = "Converged",
  psd = "Warning (PSD)",
  not_conv = "Not conv.",
  fw_c1 = "Error (C1)",
  fw_c2 = "Error (C2)",
  zero_col = "Error (zero col.)"
)
lspim_reps |>
  inner_join(lspim_scenarios, by = "scenario_id") |>
  mutate(outcome = case_when(
    grepl("clustering C1", error_message) ~ "fw_c1",
    grepl("clustering C2", error_message) ~ "fw_c2",
    grepl("all zero", error_message) ~ "zero_col",
    convergence_status == "not_converged" ~ "not_conv",
    convergence_status == "converged_warning" ~ "psd",
    convergence_status == "converged_ok" ~ "ok"
  )) |>
  mutate(outcome = factor(lspim_outcomes[outcome], levels = lspim_outcomes)) |>
  count(n, dropout_mechanism, outcome, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(n, dropout_mechanism) |>
  mutate(pct = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * nn / sum(nn))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Dropout = ifelse(dropout_mechanism == "half_missing", "HM", "3O")) |>
  select(n, Dropout, outcome, pct) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = pct) |>
  arrange(n, Dropout != "HM") |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "LSPIM outcome per replicate (% of replicates, pooled over time trends and effect sizes).",
      "PSD = V repaired to the nearest PSD matrix; C1/C2 = leverage 1 in that clustering; zero col. = all-zero design column."
    ),
    align = "l"
  )
```

-   LSPIM uses three clusterings of the pairwise pseudo-observations: by left subject (C1), by right subject (C2) and by pair (C3); the combined covariance is $V = V_{C1} + V_{C2} - V_{C3}$.
-   Errors occur almost only at $n = 10$ (about 20% of replicates):
    -   about 10% each: a cluster has leverage 1 in clustering C1 or C2, so the Ford-Westgate small-sample correction is undefined;
    -   about 1%: no between-arm pairs at one or more late visits (one arm has no observations left there), so the corresponding design columns are all zero.
-   Warnings: at $n = 10$ and $20$ nearly every fit that does not error has to repair the combined covariance $V$ to the nearest positive semi-definite matrix (negative eigenvalues or non-positive variances); about 1--2% of fits at $n = 50$, and none from $n = 100$.
-   Not converged: rare (below 1% at $n = 10$, almost none from $n = 20$); the penalised GEE gives fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1.
-   The repaired $V$ at small $n$ may contribute to LSPIM's type I error inflation at $n = 10$ and $20$.
